name: Unsecured (G0)
note: Gear as fitted, nothing secured against shock: breakers trip at a hull shock factor of 0.07 (half the time). Everyone before 1940, the RN to late 1940, the USN to early 1942; merchant-built and converted hulls throughout; the IJN and Kriegsmarine throughout [UNCERTAIN: no record of their securing work]. Before about 1910 a ship has few breakers to trip (fuses, knife switches, dynamos on their own governors).

name: Secured (G1)
note: Fuse and switch securing alterations: breakers at 0.22. The RN from late 1940 (after Southampton), the USN from 1942. Cheap: fixes and procedures, no weight.

name: Shock-tested (G2)
note: High-impact shock-tested gear on resilient mounts: breakers at 0.55 [EST]. USN new construction and refits from 1943; RN new construction from 1943 [UNCERTAIN]. +1-2% of electrical weight [EST], not built.

name: Grade-A (G3)
note: Post-war grade-A shock gear: breakers at 1.1 [EST].
